author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Cryptocurrency services company Bitcoin Suisse plans to eliminate as many as 60 of its 120 jobs in Switzerland, Reuters reported. The Zug-based firm is consulting employees through September 20 before finalizing the reductions, which would amount to as much as half of its domestic workforce.

The reorganization is intended to consolidate software development and back-office operations in international hubs, where the company says it can scale faster, reach a broader pool of workers and direct investment toward future services. Bitcoin Suisse will also close its information-technology development site in Copenhagen. The changes show how crypto companies are reassessing where they build and support increasingly software-intensive financial products.

Founded in 2013, Bitcoin Suisse employs about 200 people worldwide. Beyond Switzerland, it has operations in Liechtenstein, Abu Dhabi and Bermuda, as well as an international hub in Bratislava and another planned for Vietnam. The consultation means the maximum job-cut figure is not yet final. The company did not frame the announcement as an exit from Switzerland, where its headquarters and core crypto-finance business remain based.
dek: The crypto-services company says it may eliminate 60 roles while shifting software development and back-office work to international hubs.
headline: Bitcoin Suisse plans to cut up to half its Swiss workforce
